title: Adaptive degradation policy for tiered routing and per-region circuit breakers
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Implement an adaptive degradation and circuit-breaker subsystem integrated with smart routing so the router can automatically detect capacity/quality problems (429 spikes, timeouts, elevated error rates, latency regressions) and degrade traffic in predictable, observable ways. Scope: policy engine + runtime hooks for region selection and tier routing, per-model-variant thresholds, local vs global circuits, and safe fallback behaviors (route to dedicated capacity, demote to lower-cost quantized model variant, or return structured error with suggested retry-after). This ticket covers design, API for rules, runtime gating, metrics, dashboards, unit/chaos tests, and rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria: Policy engine supports declarative rules: rate-based (429s), latency-based (p50/p95/p99), error-rate (5xx), and timeout-based triggers
Per-region and per-tier (hosted/dedicated/private) thresholds and actions configurable via console and config-as-code
Circuit breakers: open/half-open/closed lifecycle with configurable open duration, trial window, and exponential backoff
Fallback actions available: reroute to compatible model variant, demote to quantized variant (no streaming), route to Dedicated pool, or return structured 503 with Retry-After
Router produces metrics on every decision: trigger_type, scope(region|global), source_tier, fallback_action, affected_requests
Automated canary/chaos tests demonstrate correct behavior under synthetic 429 spikes, 99th latency regression, and regional outage simulation
SLO impact report template and alerting thresholds documented and wired into console dashboards (runtime-2.4 release)
End-to-end e2e test with 5K RPS synthetic load reproduces controlled demotion and recovery without user-visible errors beyond expected fallback responses
comments: 2026-02-11 - Asha Patel: Initial triage and problem statement added. Identified primary triggers: sustained 429 spikes, repeated timeouts, >=3% 5xx over 1m window, p99 latency regressions. Asked SRE for baseline thresholds.

2026-02-18 - Miguel Ortega (SRE): Suggested local (node-level) and regional circuit separation. Proposed default open_duration=60s, half_open_probe=5 requests, backoff_multiplier=2. Also recommended per-customer override capability for Dedicated customers.
2026-02-22 - Jun Park: Drafted runtime hooks to intercept router decisions and annotate request context with 'fallback_reason'. Prototype available in feature branch routing/fallback-prototype.
2026-02-25 - Design review (DES-210): Design sign-off on UI surfaces: per-route policy config, visualization of recent triggers, and manual 'force-demote' control. Minor copy edits requested.
2026-02-27 - PM sync (Olivia Chen): Agreed rollout steps: feature-flag gate, soft-launch to internal accounts, monitor two weeks, then opt-in beta for high-traffic customers before global rollout.

2026-03-01 - Jun Park: Implemented metrics emission (counter:router.fallbacks.total, gauge:router.circuits.open, histogram:router.fallback_latency_ms). Opened PR #4890 for review and unit tests. Requesting SRE review on alert thresholds.
implementation_notes: Runtime hook will evaluate policies in priority order: region-specific rules first, then tier rules, then global defaults. For 429 spikes we will use rolling 1m and 5m windows and require sustained condition across both to avoid flapping. Circuit state persisted in distributed key-value store with TTL equal to open_duration. Half-open uses token-bucket style probes. Fallback to quantized variant will disable streaming and reduce max_tokens to limit cost. All fallback decisions annotated in request logs and surfaced to console.
risks: Risk of false-positive opens if thresholds are too tight => increased user-visible fallbacks
Complexity of per-customer overrides could cause inconsistencies across hierarchy
Metric cardinality growth from many per-model+region rules
